verdict.stance: Neutral / Sovereign-Backed Kazakh Power Generator in Heavy Capex Cycle (Baa2/BB+)
verdict.summary: Samruk-Energy (100% Samruk-Kazyna) is Kazakhstan's largest power generator (40.4bn kWh in FY25; revenue KZT 752.8bn, operating profit KZT 225.8bn, net debt KZT 495.7bn). Moody's assigned a first-time Baa2 Stable IG rating (Fitch BB+ Stable, 'b+' SCP) recognizing critical grid security and predictable capacity tariffs despite debt-funded Almaty gasification capex.

positives: 100% state-owned via Samruk-Kazyna with 'Very Likely' extraordinary support under Moody's Baa2 / Fitch BB+.
Regulated power & capacity tariff framework supports KZT 225.8bn FY25 operating profit and KZT 154.8bn net profit.
Modest current net debt (KZT 495.7bn, <2x EBITDA) prior to peak capex execution.
negatives: Multi-year debt-funded capex (Almaty CHP-2/3 gasification, Ekibastuz, renewables) drives negative FCF and rising leverage.
Fitch standalone credit profile remains 'b+', making ratings heavily reliant on state support.
FX mismatch risk if hard-currency borrowing increases against KZT tariff revenues.

background.business_overview: Kazakhstan's largest electric power holding company across thermal, hydro, coal, and renewables.
background.asset_perimeter: Ekibastuz GRES-1/2, Bogatyr Komir (50%), Almaty power stations, Moynak & Shardarinskaya HPPs.
background.ownership_governance: 100% owned by Sovereign Wealth Fund Samruk-Kazyna (Republic of Kazakhstan).
